subject: Logic
title: Arrow's Impossibility
description: A quick, practical guide to Arrow's Impossibility.

hook.text: Three friends rank pizza, sushi, and tacos differently. No voting system can always fairly combine their preferences.

buildup.text: Arrow's impossibility theorem proves no ranked voting system can satisfy all fairness criteria simultaneously.

discovery.text: Kenneth Arrow showed that with three or more options, every voting rule violates at least one reasonable fairness rule.

twist.text: This means all voting systems are imperfect—not broken, just inevitably compromised on some dimension.

climax.text: The question isn't which system is perfect. It's which tradeoffs matter most for your specific context.

quiz.question: What does Arrow's impossibility theorem prove?
options: No ranked voting system satisfies all fairness criteria
